items.headline: Woman, 49, arrested over alleged 'Fun Coffee' Ponzi scheme; one victim lost about S$400,000
items.summary: Singapore police arrested a 49-year-old woman over an alleged 'Fun Coffee' investment scam; at least one victim is believed to have lost around S$400,000.

items.headline: Singaporean reported missing in Vietnam arrested over alleged etomidate vape syndicate
items.summary: A Singaporean man once reported missing in Vietnam was arrested on his return over alleged links to a syndicate distributing etomidate-laced vapes.

items.headline: Singaporean man, 58, who fled Singapore by boat in 2002 jailed over 14 months
items.summary: A 58-year-old Singaporean who absconded by boat in 2002, then repeatedly entered and left the country illegally, was jailed for more than 14 months.

items.headline: Man, 27, jailed 19 weeks for pushing and kicking his 65-year-old mother
items.summary: A 27-year-old man was jailed 19 weeks after pushing his 65-year-old mother and kicking her in the face over a long wait for a car.

items.headline: Airbus finds hydraulic faults on Air India A320 after jet dropped about 300 feet mid-flight
items.summary: Airbus said it found hydraulic-system faults on an Air India A320 that lost about 300 feet on a Phuket-to-Delhi flight before the crew restored control.

items.headline: Tata Steel sells ISL football club Jamshedpur FC to Churchill Brothers for $1
items.summary: Tata Steel is selling Indian Super League club Jamshedpur FC to Goa's Churchill Brothers for a token $1, transferring the ISL licence, 12 players and two coaches.

items.headline: 'My own country called me a national security threat,' says India's 'Cockroach' movement founder
items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenging Modi's BJP, told CNN's Christiane Amanpour he was branded a national security threat as protests over jobs and exam leaks persist.

items.headline: Goldman and Nomura say AI is more likely to reshape India's jobs than destroy them
items.summary: Economists at Goldman Sachs and Nomura argue generative AI will more likely change tasks within India's white-collar jobs than eliminate them, though the shift adds pressure amid high graduate unemployment.

items.headline: Rupee stability could help India draw more foreign investment, analysts say
items.summary: With the rupee steadier after a volatile stretch, analysts say calmer currency swings could make Indian assets more attractive to overseas investors.

items.headline: Nigel Farage wins Clacton by-election, beating novelty candidate Count Binface
items.summary: Farage reclaimed Clacton with 62.8% (22,239 votes); joke candidate Count Binface took a record 26.7% (9,455) in a 34-candidate field after the main parties boycotted the vote he triggered by resigning during a probe into an unreported £5m gift.

items.headline: UK petrol and diesel prices jump more than 20% since the Iran war as living costs bite
items.summary: An Al Jazeera analysis found UK petrol up about 22% and diesel about 27% since late February as the Iran war lifted energy costs; June inflation was 2.8%, and the Bank of England expects it to climb again.

items.headline: Burnham shifts Britain's centre of power north toward Manchester
items.summary: Since Andy Burnham became prime minister, his government has leaned into devolution and a 'smaller, strategic' central state, shifting political gravity toward Manchester and the north, Bloomberg analysis said.

items.headline: UAE accuses Iran of drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The UAE said Iran launched drone attacks on two ADNOC-operated tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 14, calling it 'piracy'; there were no casualties and only minor damage.

items.headline: Japan protests as Putin visits the disputed Kuril Islands
items.summary: Tokyo lodged a formal protest after Russian President Vladimir Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands, which Japan claims as its Northern Territories.

items.headline: US accuses dozens of countries of helping China evade Trump's tariffs
items.summary: The US accused dozens of countries of acting as transshipment hubs that help Chinese goods dodge Trump-era tariffs, threatening penalties as trade tensions widen.

items.headline: Wildfires force thousands to flee as blazes spread across Europe
items.summary: Wildfires fanned by heat and drought forced thousands to evacuate across parts of Europe, straining firefighting crews during a punishing summer.

items.headline: IBM partners with OpenAI to bring GPT-5.6 and Codex to enterprise clients
items.summary: IBM said it will build a dedicated OpenAI practice in its consulting arm and fold GPT-5.6, Codex and ChatGPT Work into its tools, training tens of thousands of consultants to deploy OpenAI models for big companies.

items.headline: Databricks raises $5 billion at a $190 billion valuation
items.summary: Databricks closed a $5 billion round led by Coatue at a $190 billion valuation, up from $134 billion in February, saying it crossed a $7 billion revenue run rate with over 80% year-on-year growth.

items.headline: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2 billion to fold AI into traditional businesses
items.summary: Thrive Holdings, an OpenAI-backed firm that buys traditional companies and rebuilds them around AI, raised $2 billion from investors including SoftBank at a $12 billion valuation.

items.headline: Anthropic in talks to buy AI-efficiency startup Decart for about $6 billion
items.summary: Anthropic is in talks to acquire Decart, whose software makes AI chips run more efficiently and builds 'world models,' for about $6 billion — what would be its largest known acquisition, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: US retail sales fell 0.6% in July, the biggest drop since May 2025
items.summary: US retail sales dropped 0.6% in July, the steepest fall since May 2025, dragged by a 1.8% slide in vehicle sales and softer online spending, though still up about 5% from a year earlier.

items.headline: US consumer sentiment slid to 51 in August, its first decline in three months
items.summary: The University of Michigan's preliminary sentiment index fell to 51.0 in August from 55.2, its first drop in three months, as households worried about business conditions and inflation.

items.headline: Applied Materials' upbeat forecast draws a tepid reaction as shares slip
items.summary: Applied Materials guided to about $10.3 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, above the roughly $9.6 billion expected, but its shares slipped as investors had priced in even more from the AI chip-gear supplier.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs's newest cash cow: financing the AI infrastructure boom
items.summary: CNBC reported Goldman Sachs is increasingly profiting from arranging financing for the AI data-center buildout, using compute infrastructure as cash-generating collateral as banks race to fund the boom.

items.headline: Shelton defends his National Bank Open title in an all-American Montreal final
items.summary: Ben Shelton beat fellow American Brandon Nakashima 6-3, 7-6(4) to defend his National Bank Open crown in Montreal without dropping a set all week.

items.headline: Swiatek beats Rybakina in Toronto for her first title of 2026
items.summary: Iga Swiatek downed Elena Rybakina 6-2, 6-3 to win the National Bank Open in Toronto, claiming her 26th career title and first of 2026 after a nearly year-long drought.

items.headline: The Hundred reaches Finals Day with Trent Rockets awaiting their Lord's opponent
items.summary: Trent Rockets, who topped the men's group, go straight to the Aug 16 Lord's final, where they will meet the winner of Friday's Kia Oval Eliminator between Manchester Super Giants and SunRisers Leeds.

items.headline: Cadillac sack Graeme Lowdon and name Marcin Budkowski team principal
items.summary: F1 newcomer Cadillac dismissed team principal Graeme Lowdon and appointed former Alpine executive Marcin Budkowski, who takes over the still point-less team ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix (Aug 21-23).

items.headline: Physicists report the strongest evidence yet for a 'glueball' made purely of gluons
items.summary: Physicists at China's BESIII experiment reported compelling evidence that the particle X(2370) is largely a 'glueball' — a knot of gluons with no quarks — a long-predicted state confirming gluons can bind to themselves.

items.headline: Engineered gut probiotics sense high blood sugar and treat diabetes in mice and monkeys
items.summary: Researchers built probiotic bacteria with a glucose-sensing genetic circuit that release therapeutic factors only when blood sugar rises; the oral 'living therapy' improved glycaemic control in diabetic mice and monkeys, per Nature.

items.headline: Scientists explain how metformin works: it turns the gut into a 'sugar sink'
items.summary: A new study suggests the widely used diabetes drug metformin lowers blood sugar largely by prompting gut cells to soak up more glucose, helping resolve a decades-old mystery about its main mechanism.

items.headline: Total solar eclipse sweeps across Iceland and Spain, the first over Spain since 1905
items.summary: A total solar eclipse on Aug 12 crossed Greenland, Iceland and Spain with up to 2 minutes 18 seconds of totality; it was the first total eclipse visible from Spain since 1905.

notes: India ran on the fallback tier (Bloomberg, CNN): the six primary Indian outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times) are blocked to the search crawler and unreachable via WebFetch (egress 403). Five India-domestic items were sourced from allowed fallback outlets, clearing the floor.

India's 80th Independence Day (Aug 15): PM Modi's Red Fort address and the first-ever Vande Mataram rendition were scheduled for ~10:00 SGT, after this run's start time, and no allowed-list outlet had published the speech content yet, so it was held rather than reported unverified. Confirmed pre-event facts (about 15,000 security personnel, ~1,000 CCTV cameras, anti-drone systems) were corroborated only via off-list Indian outlets and so were not carried.

UK ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) and below the 4-item floor at 3 items: primary outlets BBC and Sky News are unreachable from this environment (search-domain filters + egress 403). Three retry attempts were made across both primary outlets before switching. Only three UK-domestic stories (Farage's Clacton by-election, the cost-of-living/fuel-price analysis, and Burnham's devolution shift) could be tied to an allowed-list outlet with adequate recency; older items (NHS-Palantir review, Burnham migration) were dropped rather than date-stretched.

Singapore ran on Mothership only (CNA and The Straits Times are crawler-blocked; SCMP surfaced no fresh Aug 13-14 domestic story). The reachable window was dominated by court/crime; four such items were carried straight. The Workers' Party future-economy motion (Aug 5) and Pritam Singh's National Day message (~Aug 8-9) were outside the 48-72h window and dropped.

Global ran entirely on Al Jazeera (an allowed Global outlet); all four items are major wire-covered stories corroborated across outlets that could not be linked from this environment (BBC/Reuters/AP egress-blocked).

Sports: the National Bank Open finals (Shelton in Montreal, Swiatek in Toronto, both played late Aug 13 local / Aug 14 SGT) were verified via ESPN and WTA. The Hundred men's Eliminator (Manchester Super Giants v SunRisers Leeds, Kia Oval, Aug 14 D/N) had no allowed-source confirmed final result at run time, so the item was framed around the confirmed Finals Day structure (Trent Rockets await their Aug 16 Lord's opponent) without asserting an unverified winner. F1 is between rounds (Dutch GP resumes Aug 21-23), so the F1 item carries the Cadillac team-principal change rather than a stale race recap.
US markets: the retail-sales and consumer-sentiment prints (both Aug 14) were the marquee macro data; prior-day items (S&P record close, oil/OPEC) were not repeated.
No missed prior run: archive/2026-08-14 exists.

fun_fact.headline: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire
fun_fact.body: The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching at Oxford dates back to at least 1096, and the university was well established by 1167 — more than two centuries before the Aztecs founded their capital, Tenochtitlan, in 1325, and long before the Aztec Empire itself arose in 1428.
fun_fact.source: University of Oxford (institutional history); Smithsonian Magazine

puzzle.title: Wine and Water
puzzle.body: Two equal glasses, one wine and one water. Move a spoonful of wine into the water and stir; then move a spoonful of the mixture back into the wine. Is there more water in the wine, more wine in the water, or are they equal?
puzzle.approach: Don't chase the mixing — track what has to balance out; each glass returns to its original volume.
puzzle.answer: They are exactly equal. Each glass ends at its original volume, so the wine missing from the wine glass has been replaced by exactly that much water, and that displaced wine sits in the water glass — equal amounts either way, regardless of spoon size or stirring.

word_puzzle.title: Count on It
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange all the letters of ELEVEN PLUS TWO into a different arithmetic phrase that uses exactly the same letters and equals the same total.
word_puzzle.approach: Every letter is reused — none added or dropped — to write the same total another way.
word_puzzle.answer: TWELVE PLUS ONE. Both phrases use the identical thirteen letters (three E's, two L's, and one each of N, O, P, S, T, U, V, W) and both equal 13.
